title: Keep the app bar to one short line
intent: Protect working height and keep the primary surface reachable without a scroll.
when_to_use: a tool surface the user operates for long sessions
the nav carries one wordmark, one product switcher, and at most four destinations
when_not_to_use: the surface is a marketing site with a long destination list, where the fix is a different family rather than a taller bar
the layout is a rail based shell, where navigation lives in the rail and the bar stays nearly empty
rules: the nav element is at most 80px tall on desktop and never wraps to two lines
destinations beyond four move into a menu or into a rail, never into a second row
no build number, version string, or environment label appears in a shipped marketing nav or footer
the wordmark is a mark or set type; a row of typed company names is not a logo wall
app bar and account menu icons come from one family at one stroke width, and no emoji is used as an interface icon
trade_off: Folding destinations into a menu lowers their discovery, so secondary surfaces get fewer visits and turn into documentation problems instead of product paths.
failure_mode: The bar creeps: a beta badge, a status pill, then a second row for modules, until the working area loses 40 pixels on a laptop and the first content row is below the fold.

example.brief: Internal analytics tool used for hours at a time.
example.ruling: Nav is a single 64px row: mark, four destinations, account menu. The beta badge moves into the product menu and the footer keeps only links and support contact.
